/-!
# Erdős Problem 572

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/572](https://www.erdosproblems.com/572)
- [Er64c] Erdős, P., Extremal problems in graph theory. Theory of Graphs and its
  Applications (1964), 29-36.
- [BoSi74] Bondy, J. A. and Simonovits, M., Cycles of even length in graphs.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (1974), 97-105.
- [LUW95] Lazebnik, F., Ustimenko, V. A. and Woldar, A. J., A new series of dense graphs
  of high girth. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1995), 73-79.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos572

/--
Show that for $k\geq 3$
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;C_{2k})\gg n^{1+\frac{1}{k}}.$$

This problem is #46 in Extremal Graph Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_572 (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + 1 / (k : ℝ)) ≤
        (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph (2 * k)) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos572

reformulations.difference: The source’s Vinogradov lower bound is expanded into an explicit positive real constant and an eventual inequality on natural numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For fixed k, both n^(1+1/k) and the extremal number are nonnegative. Thus ex(n;C_(2k)) ≫ n^(1+1/k) means that some C>0 eventually satisfies n^(1+1/k) ≤ C·ex(n;C_(2k)). Taking c=1/C gives precisely the Lean inequality, and conversely taking C=1/c recovers the source bound. On ℕ, eventually atTop is equivalent to holding for all n beyond some threshold. These equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the conjecture’s sorry-backed theorem.

review.notes: The file’s sole theorem faithfully states the cited conjecture. Mathlib’s extremalNumber maximizes ordinary edge counts over graphs excluding non-induced copies, as required. The restriction k≥3 ensures 2k≥6, avoiding degenerate cycle definitions; the empty graph always belongs to the admissible family. Scratch checks computed small cycle edge counts and proved extremalNumber n (cycleGraph m) = n.choose 2 when n<m, including the zero- and one-vertex cases. The source still records the general conjecture as OPEN; the known cases k=3,5 do not make the theorem’s category stale. All scratch checks compile without errors or warnings.
